resources.how: Check your rights and find the forms on nav.no, or contact your regional assistive technology centre (hjelpemiddelsentral). Nav’s phone line is open weekdays, 9:00 to 11:15 and 12:15 to 14:30. In Norwegian.

resources.name: Equality and Anti-Discrimination Ombud (LDO)
resources.what: Free guidance for anyone who thinks they have been discriminated against, including because of a disability. Employers and organisations can ask too.
resources.how: Call the advice line Monday to Thursday, 12:30 to 14:30, or Friday, 9:00 to 11:00, or write through its secure contact forms. Its site has a page in English.

emergency.label: Ambulance, fire and police. For non-urgent police matters, call 114

resources.name: Livslinien
resources.what: An anonymous line for people with thoughts of suicide and for those worried about someone. It is open every day of the year from 9:00 to 5:00 the next morning, not around the clock. A chat is open in the evenings and weekend afternoons.
resources.how: Call 70 201 201 between 9:00 and 5:00. Chat runs Monday to Friday, 17:00 to 21:00, and Saturday and Sunday, 13:00 to 17:00. Its website is in Danish.

resources.name: Disability pension (førtidspension)
resources.org: Your municipality (kommune); paid by Udbetaling Danmark
resources.what: For people whose ability to work is permanently reduced so much that they cannot work on ordinary terms. You must meet residence rules. The municipality decides, after a resource clarification process and a rehabilitation plan made with you.
resources.how: Contact your municipality to start. Once it is granted, Udbetaling Danmark pays it to your NemKonto. The life in Denmark guide explains it in English.

resources.name: Support for a car (støtte til handicapbil)
resources.what: An interest-free loan towards the cheapest suitable car (up to 231,000 kroner in 2026) for people whose lasting physical or mental disability makes them depend on a car to work, study or take part in activities. You can also get help with adaptations such as hand controls or a swivel seat, and with driving lessons. Parents can apply for a disabled child.
resources.how: Apply to your municipality through the “Ansøg om støtte til bil” self-service on borger.dk, or contact the municipality if you cannot apply online. In Danish.

resources.name: Diskriminationslinjen (Discrimination Helpline)
resources.what: Free legal advice if you have been discriminated against, including because of a disability, or are unsure whether you have. Its lawyers can help with complaints to the Equal Treatment Board (Ligebehandlingsnævnet).
resources.how: Call Monday to Thursday, 12:00 to 15:00, or email diskriminationslinjen@humanrights.dk with “Diskriminationslinjen” in the subject. In Danish.

emergency.label: European emergency number, answered by the police control centre. Ambulance: 144. Fire: 118. Police: 117

resources.name: Die Dargebotene Hand / La Main Tendue (Tel 143)
resources.what: An anonymous listening line open 24 hours a day for anyone who needs to talk. An English-language crisis line runs every evening.
resources.how: Call 143, any hour; a call costs 20 to 70 centimes. In German, French or Italian. In English, call 0800 143 000, daily from 18:00 to 23:00.

resources.name: Pro Infirmis social counselling
resources.what: Free counselling for disabled people and their relatives across Switzerland, covering housing, work, money and daily life, with a centre in every canton.
resources.how: Choose your canton on the Pro Infirmis website to find the advice centre near you. In German, French or Italian, and in easy language.

resources.name: Disability insurance (Invalidenversicherung IV / assurance-invalidité AI)
resources.org: The IV office of your canton
resources.what: Compulsory insurance for everyone living or working in Switzerland. It pays first for help to stay in or return to work, medical measures and aids such as a wheelchair or hearing aid; a pension if you are on average at least 40% unable to work for a year; a helplessness allowance if you need help with daily tasks; and an assistance contribution to help you keep living at home.
resources.how: Register with the IV office of the canton where you live (cross-border workers: where you work) on the registration form. Do not wait: a late registration can cost you benefits. In German, French or Italian.

resources.name: Procap legal advice on social insurance
resources.what: Advice and legal support on disability insurance (IV), accident insurance, occupational pensions and supplementary benefits. It is free for Procap members.
resources.how: Call the legal service, or find a regional advice centre on procap.ch. Non-members can ask about the terms. In German.

emergency.label: Ambulance (Rettung). For the police, call 133

resources.name: TelefonSeelsorge (Notruf 142)
resources.what: A free listening line open every day around the clock, with email and chat counselling too.
resources.how: Call 142, any hour; there is no charge from any phone in Austria. In German.

resources.name: Disability pass (Behindertenpass)
resources.what: An official photo ID that proves a degree of disability of at least 50%. It brings discounts, and from 70% a half-price fare on Austrian Federal Railways (ÖBB). It is also the first step to the disabled parking card. It pays no money itself.
resources.how: Apply to the regional office of the Sozialministeriumservice with a photo and your medical records or earlier decisions. If you have no assessment yet, an SMS doctor estimates your degree of disability, usually from your documents. In German.

resources.name: Care allowance (Pflegegeld)
resources.what: A monthly allowance, in seven levels, for people who need more than 65 hours of care and support a month because of a physical, mental, psychological or sensory disability expected to last at least six months, whatever the cause. You must normally live in Austria.
resources.how: The responsible body sets your level after an expert assessment, usually an announced home visit by a doctor or nurse. The government’s help portal explains where to apply. In German.

resources.name: Disabled parking card (Parkausweis nach § 29b StVO)
resources.what: A parking card for people whose disability pass carries the entry that they cannot use public transport because of a permanent loss of mobility. In most provinces, cardholders park free.
resources.how: Apply to the Sozialministeriumservice on its digital or paper form with a passport photo. The government portal has the details in English.

resources.name: Federal Disability Ombudsperson (Behindertenanwältin)
resources.org: Anwaltschaft für Gleichbehandlungsfragen für Menschen mit Behinderungen
resources.what: Free advice, support and representation if you feel you have been discriminated against because of a disability under federal equality or employment law. It can also run conciliation proceedings for you at the Sozialministeriumservice.
resources.how: Call free on 0800 80 80 16, every day from 9:00 to 12:00, email office@behindertenanwalt.gv.at, or come to a consultation day in your province. In German.

countries.name: Japan

emergency.label: Fire and ambulance. For the police, call 110

countries.relay: Deaf or speech-impaired: where your local fire department has joined Net119, you can report a fire or medical emergency from your phone’s browser and continue by text chat.

resources.name: Yorisoi Hotline (よりそいホットライン)
resources.org: Listed by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
resources.what: A free line open 24 hours a day for any worry. The recorded guidance lets you choose specialist help, including help in foreign languages.
resources.how: Call 0120-279-338, free. From Fukushima Prefecture, call 0120-279-226; from an IP phone, 050-3655-0279. Choose a foreign language in the guidance if you need one.

resources.name: TELL Lifeline
resources.what: A free, confidential English-language support line for anyone in Japan, with chat as well. It is not open around the clock.
resources.how: Call 0800-300-8355, free. Phone hours: Saturday 9:00 through Monday 23:00, Tuesday to Thursday 9:00 to 23:00, and Friday 9:00 to 2:00. Chat opens daily from 16:00. In English.

resources.name: Disability certificates (障害者手帳)
resources.org: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare; your city, town or village office
resources.what: Three certificates: for physical disability (身体障害者手帳), intellectual disability (療育手帳) and mental illness (精神障害者保健福祉手帳). Any of them opens support under the Comprehensive Support Act for persons with disabilities, and they bring discounts such as reduced JR fares and toll roads, depending on the certificate.
resources.how: Ask the disability welfare desk at your city, town or village office. The physical disability certificate needs a report from a designated doctor and a photo. In Japanese.

resources.name: Human rights consultation line (みんなの人権110番)
resources.org: Ministry of Justice human rights bureaus
resources.what: A national phone line for advice about human rights problems, including discrimination against disabled people.
resources.how: Call weekdays, 8:30 to 17:15. In Japanese.

emergency.label: Fire, disasters and medical emergencies, answered by the National Fire Agency. You can also report to 119 by text message with photos, through the 119 reporting app or by video call

resources.name: Suicide prevention line 109 (자살예방 상담전화)
resources.org: Government of the Republic of Korea
resources.what: The national suicide prevention counselling line, answered by trained counsellors 24 hours a day.
resources.how: Call 109, any hour. The government page describing it is in Korean and does not say which other languages are offered.

resources.name: Health and Welfare Call Centre 129 (보건복지상담센터)
resources.what: The national line for questions about health and welfare programmes, including the disability pension. There is also a chat with its counsellors.
resources.how: Call 129 with no area code. In Korean.

resources.name: Disability pension (장애인연금)
resources.what: A monthly pension for severely disabled people aged 18 or over on low incomes and assets (in 2025, up to 1.38 million won a month for a single person). It paid up to 432,510 won a month in 2025.
resources.how: Apply at your local community service centre (읍·면·동 행정복지센터) or online through Bokjiro. Questions: call 129. In Korean.

resources.name: National Human Rights Commission of Korea
resources.org: National Human Rights Commission of Korea (NHRCK)
resources.what: Takes complaints about unlawful discrimination, including because of a disability, under the Act on the Prohibition of Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities.
resources.how: Call 1331 in Seoul and Gyeonggi, or 02-1331 elsewhere. You can also send a complaint by mail, fax or email to hoso@humanrights.go.kr; an English complaint form is on its site.

countries.name: Israel

emergency.label: Magen David Adom ambulance. Police: 100. Fire and rescue: 102

countries.relay: Deaf or speech-impaired: you can reach Magen David Adom by text message at 052-7000101 or by fax at 1-800-500-101.

resources.name: ERAN emotional first aid
resources.what: A volunteer emotional support line, open 24 hours a day, every day of the year, anonymously. Chat, WhatsApp and text are open from 8:00 to 2:00 in Hebrew, Arabic and Russian.
resources.how: Call 1201, any hour. The phone line is in Hebrew; for other languages, use the chat or ERAN’s helpline for new immigrants.

resources.name: General disability pension
resources.what: A monthly pension for residents from 18 to retirement age who do not work or earn little, with a medical disability of at least 60% (or 40% with several impairments) set by a National Insurance doctor, and whose earning capacity is reduced by at least half.
resources.how: Claim online or at a branch by appointment. The call centre is *6050, or 04-8812345. Its site explains the pension in English.

emergency.label: ECU 911, the single emergency number, free and open 24 hours a day

resources.name: Mental health line 171, option 6
resources.what: The health ministry’s mental health line, answered by specialist staff every day including holidays, from 7:00 to 20:00. It is not open around the clock; at other times, call the emergency number.
resources.how: Call 171 and choose option 6, between 7:00 and 20:00. In Spanish.

resources.name: Disability certificate (calificación de discapacidad)
resources.what: The free medical, psychological and social assessment that certifies a disability of 30% or more, for Ecuadorians and foreigners living in Ecuador. It opens the door to disability benefits and aids, and your ID card can then show your disability at no cost.
resources.how: After a clinical assessment, the health professional sets your appointment at an MSP health centre. Bring the signed application, your ID or passport and reports from authorised professionals. Deaf people can book by video with sign-language help: call 171, option 4, 8:00 to 14:00. In Spanish.

resources.name: Joaquín Gallegos Lara benefit (Bono Joaquín Gallegos Lara)
resources.what: A monthly payment of 240 dollars, made to the person who cares for someone with a severe disability (intellectual or psychosocial 65% or more, physical 75% or more), a catastrophic or rare illness, or a child with HIV, who lives in critical economic hardship or extreme poverty.
resources.how: Take the beneficiary’s ID, a recent utility bill, a sketch of how to find the home and the disability certificate to your nearest district office, weekdays 8:00 to 16:30. It is free. In Spanish.

resources.name: Wheelchairs and other aids (ayudas técnicas)
resources.what: Free wheelchairs, canes, prostheses, orthoses and other aids for people with a certified disability who need them, after a prescription from an MSP health professional. A home visit is possible if you cannot travel.
resources.how: Call 171, option 4, and say it is for an aid prescription. Go to your appointment, then collect the aid from the provincial office. In Spanish.

resources.name: National Council for Disability Equality (CONADIS)
resources.org: Consejo Nacional para la Igualdad de Discapacidades
resources.what: Free advice and guidance when the rights of a disabled person are threatened or violated, for disabled people, their families and anyone in Ecuador.
resources.how: Use the online form, email informacion@consejodiscapacidades.gob.ec, or visit the Quito office or a provincial office, weekdays 8:00 to 16:30. In Spanish.

emergency.label: Emergencies that threaten life, property or the environment. You can also report through the Emergencias 9-1-1 CR app

resources.name: Línea Aquí Estoy
resources.org: Colegio de Profesionales en Psicología de Costa Rica
resources.what: A free emotional support line from the professional college of psychologists. It is not open around the clock; in an emergency, call the emergency number.
resources.how: Call 800-AQESTOY (800-2737869), Monday to Friday 14:00 to 22:00, or Saturday 9:00 to 16:00.

resources.name: Defensoría de los Habitantes
resources.org: Defensoría de los Habitantes de la República
resources.what: The national ombudsman. It takes complaints when a public institution fails or violates people’s rights, and it is the national body that monitors the UN disability convention. Most of the disability complaints it receives concern health services, pensions and due process.
resources.how: Call free on 800-258-7474 (switchboard 4000-8500), email correspondencia@dhr.go.cr, use the complaint form on its website, or visit its San José office. In Spanish.

emergency.label: The single emergency number for police, ambulance, fire and emergency social services, free and open 24 hours a day

resources.name: MIELI Crisis Helpline (Kriisipuhelin)
resources.what: Crisis support by phone. The Finnish-language line is open 24 hours a day, every day; there are also lines in Swedish and English.
resources.how: Call 09 2525 0111 for Finnish, at any hour. Swedish: 09 2525 0112. English: 09 2525 0116, Mondays 16:00 to 20:00 and Thursdays and Fridays 9:00 to 13:00. MIELI does not charge for calls; your operator’s normal rate applies.

resources.name: Disability allowance for persons aged 16 or over
resources.org: Kela (the Social Insurance Institution of Finland)
resources.what: A tax-free monthly payment when a doctor has diagnosed a chronic illness or disability that limits your functioning for at least 12 months and brings extra costs or a need for help or guidance. Your income and assets do not affect it. There are three rates: €110.49, €257.82 and €499.93 a month. From 1 January 2027 the lower age limit rises to 18.
resources.how: Apply in the OmaKela e-service on form EV 256e with a medical statement (BC) issued in the last 6 months, or by post, by phone or at a Kela service point. Kela can pay up to 6 months back. Kela publishes its instructions in English.

resources.name: Parking card for people with reduced mobility
resources.what: A personal card that lets the vehicle you are driving or riding in park in disabled spaces, in paid spaces free of charge and in some no-parking areas. A doctor must assess that you cannot move around independently, or your sight must be severely impaired; it can also be issued to someone who often has to be driven and cannot manage alone afterwards. A Finnish card can be used in all EU countries.
resources.how: Get a medical certificate on Traficom form F123, then apply in Traficom’s My e-Services (Personal services, then Services for people with reduced mobility) and pay the fee there, or apply in person at an Ajovarma service point by appointment. Applications sent by post are not processed. The card arrives by post in about two weeks. You can apply for exemption from the base vehicle tax at the same time.

resources.name: Non-Discrimination Ombudsman (Yhdenvertaisuusvaltuutettu)
resources.what: Advice and instructions about discrimination, including on the basis of disability or state of health, and help investigating suspected cases.
resources.how: Call the customer service line, Tuesdays to Thursdays 10:00 to 12:00. In Finnish, Swedish or English, and other languages if needed; sign-language users can send a video by email.

countries.name: Greece

emergency.label: The single European emergency number for the police, fire service, coastguard and ambulance (EKAV), free and open 24 hours a day. Operators answer in Greek, English and French

countries.relay: Deaf or speech-impaired: you can also reach 112 by text message (SMS or MMS), or by email at contact@112.gov.gr.

resources.name: Line 197 for urgent psychosocial support
resources.what: A free national line for adults and families in crisis, answered by social workers and psychologists 24 hours a day, every day of the year. It offers counselling and emotional support, information on welfare and mental health services, and can arrange urgent social help. It also takes reports of neglect or abuse of older or disabled adults.
resources.how: Call 197, free from landlines and mobiles, at any hour.

resources.name: Suicide intervention line 1018
resources.what: A suicide intervention line open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
resources.how: Call 1018 from a mobile or landline anywhere in Greece, at the local call rate.

resources.name: Mobility allowance (επίδομα κίνησης)
resources.org: OPEKA (Organisation of Welfare Benefits and Social Solidarity)
resources.what: A welfare allowance for people certified with a disability of 80% or more because of amputation of both legs or both arms, or paralysis of both legs, who live legally and permanently in Greece and do not get a mobility allowance from another body.
resources.how: Apply in person or by post through a municipal Community Centre (Κέντρο Κοινότητας) or an OPEKA regional office, with your ID, a signed declaration, a Greek bank account in your name and your disability certification (the KEPA decision). It cannot be done online. It is free. In Greek.

emergency.label: The single European emergency number, free and open 24 hours a day. Ambulance: 155, fire: 150, police: 158

resources.name: First psychological aid line (linka první psychické pomoci)
resources.org: 116 123, a European helpline number listed on the government portal
resources.what: A first psychological aid line, open around the clock. Calls to 116 numbers are free.
resources.how: Call 116 123, free, at any hour.

resources.name: Care allowance (příspěvek na péči)
resources.org: Úřad práce ČR (Labour Office) and the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs
resources.what: A monthly payment for people from age one who, because of a long-term health condition, need help with basic needs such as getting around, communicating, eating or personal hygiene. It is set by degree of dependency: for adults 1,300, 5,400 or 14,800 Kč, and 23,000 or 27,000 Kč at the highest degree; for under-18s 4,900, 8,200 or 16,100 Kč, and 23,000 or 27,000 Kč.
resources.how: Apply in writing on the ministry’s form at a Labour Office contact point for where you have permanent residence, saying who will help you. A social worker visits you at home before your degree of dependency is assessed. The Labour Office call centre is free. In Czech.

resources.name: Public Defender of Rights (Veřejný ochránce práv)
resources.what: The ombudsman assesses whether you were discriminated against, including because of disability, explains your rights, and if it recommends going to court may arrange free legal representation.
resources.how: Call the hotline every day, 8:00 to 16:00, email podatelna@ochrance.cz, or write to Údolní 39, 602 00 Brno. Describe what happened and keep any evidence.

countries.name: Romania

emergency.label: The single emergency number for police, fire, ambulance, SMURD and gendarmerie, free from fixed and mobile phones. Calls are also taken in the main international languages

countries.relay: Deaf or speech-impaired: if you have registered in advance with the national 112 system, call 112 from your registered mobile and then report the emergency by free text message to 113.

resources.name: TelVerde Antisuicid
resources.org: Alianța Română de Prevenție a Suicidului (ARPS)
resources.what: A free counselling line for adults at risk of suicide, run by a non-profit. It is not open around the clock; at other times, call the emergency number.
resources.how: Call 0800 801 200, free, on Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 19:00 to 07:00.

resources.name: Disability certificate (certificat de încadrare în grad de handicap)
resources.org: ANPD and the DGASPC of your county or Bucharest sector
resources.what: The assessment that sets your degree of disability and opens the payments and facilities below. The assessment can be done at home if you cannot travel.
resources.how: Send your file to the DGASPC where you live, in person, by registered post or by email, or through your town hall: the application form, ID, a social inquiry from the town hall, proof of income, a current report from your specialist and, the first time, a letter from your family doctor. You are assessed within 60 days and the certificate is posted to you. In Romanian.

resources.name: Monthly allowance and complementary personal budget
resources.org: ANPD (Autoritatea Națională pentru Protecția Drepturilor Persoanelor cu Dizabilități)
resources.what: Adults with a severe (grav) degree get a monthly allowance of 419 lei plus a complementary personal budget of 180 lei; a marked (accentuat) degree brings 317 lei plus 132 lei; a medium degree brings a personal budget of 72 lei. Income does not affect them. Severe and marked degrees also bring free urban public transport and free intercity trips each year, and parking is free in spaces reserved for disabled people.
resources.how: These rights come with the disability certificate above. In Romanian.

emergency.label: The single emergency number for police, health emergencies, fire, gendarmerie, coast guard, forest fires and AFAD, free from home, mobile and pay phones at any time

resources.name: ALO 183 Social Support Line
resources.org: Ministry of Family and Social Services
resources.what: Guidance and counselling about services for families, women, children, disabled and older people, and a line to report neglect, abuse or violence; urgent cases are passed to emergency teams. Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
resources.how: Call 183, free from inside Turkey. Calls are also answered in Kurdish and Arabic. Deaf and speech-impaired callers can make a sign-language video call to 0 549 381 0 183 (weekdays 8:00 to 24:00, Saturdays 8:00 to 17:00) or send a free SMS to 183 with name, ID number and request.

resources.name: Home care support (evde bakım desteği)
resources.org: Ministry of Family and Social Services
resources.what: Support for the care at home of a person with a severe disability (marked “ağır engelli” on the hospital disability health board report) who cannot live without another person’s help, when the household’s average income per person is below two-thirds of the monthly net minimum wage.
resources.how: Apply to the Provincial Directorate of Family and Social Services or the Social Service Centre where the disabled person lives, or to the District Governorship where there is neither. You need the disability health board report, a care board report and an income test. In Turkish.

resources.name: Complaints about disability discrimination
resources.org: Human Rights and Equality Institution of Türkiye (TİHEK) and the Ombudsman Institution (KDK)
resources.what: If you think you were discriminated against because of disability in education, justice, health, transport, social services or similar services, you can apply to TİHEK free of charge. For discrimination by a public body you can also apply free of charge to the Ombudsman Institution (KDK). Discrimination can also be reported to the police or a prosecutor as a crime.
resources.how: The ministry’s guidance page explains the routes; apply to TİHEK or the KDK directly. In Turkish.

emergency.label: Police. For an ambulance, call 998; for the fire department (Civil Defence), call 997

resources.name: 800 SAKINA mental health support line
resources.org: Department of Health – Abu Dhabi, with Sakina (SEHA)
resources.what: A mental health support line open 24 hours a day to anyone in the community, offering psychological first aid and access to qualified mental health professionals for anxiety, panic, stress and sleep problems, with services for children and families.
resources.how: Call 800 725462 (800-SAKINA), at any hour. In Arabic or English.

resources.name: People of Determination card
resources.what: A personal card issued by the ministry to people with disabilities (called people of determination in the UAE), so they can take part in education, work, health care and social life on equal terms.
resources.how: Apply to the ministry with your Emirates ID, a passport-style photo on a white background, and a medical or psychological diagnosis report approved by a People of Determination welfare and rehabilitation centre. The ministry’s line is toll-free.

emergency.label: Ambulance. For the police, call 122; for fire and civil defence, call 180

resources.name: Psychological support hotline 105
resources.org: Ministry of Health and Population (mental health and addiction treatment administration)
resources.what: Consultations by phone from psychiatrists, psychologists, social workers and nurses, 24 hours a day, every day. The ministry’s mental health line was joined to 105 in March 2026.
resources.how: Call 105, at any hour.

resources.name: National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPD)
resources.org: National Council for Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: Takes complaints and questions from disabled people and their families across Egypt, studies them legally and follows them up with government and private bodies. Its complaints portal lets you track a complaint, and it takes requests for sign-language interpretation.
resources.how: Call the hotline 16736, call 02 2453 0081, email info@ncpd.gov.eg, or register a complaint on the council’s complaints portal with your national ID number, phone number and email, a clear account of the problem and a photo of your ID card. In Arabic.

emergency.label: The single emergency number joining police, ambulance and fire, brought in across districts and cities in stages

resources.name: Healing119 mental health line
resources.what: Free emotional support and basic consultation from licensed health workers, 24 hours a day, for Indonesian citizens. If you cannot get through, the lines may be busy.
resources.how: Call 119 and choose extension 8, or use the call or WhatsApp button on the healing119.id website. No registration is needed.

resources.name: Ministry of Social Affairs command centre 171
resources.what: The ministry’s command centre number. Disabled people can call it to ask for help: in one case the ministry describes, a blind caller was assessed by a regional centre and given an adaptive cane and business capital under its ATENSI programme.
resources.how: Call 171. The ministry’s page does not give hours or call costs.

emergency.label: Emergency medical services. The general emergency hotline is 191

resources.name: Mental health hotline 1323
resources.what: Free mental health consultation with experts, open 24 hours a day, every day, for people in Thailand and visitors. English-language services are available for foreign nationals.
resources.how: Call 1323, free, at any hour.

resources.name: Welfare help for people with disabilities
resources.org: Ministry of Social Development and Human Security
resources.what: Registered people with disabilities facing hardship, such as living alone or without family support, can ask for help in goods or cash of up to 3,000 baht at a time, up to 3 times a year.
resources.how: Apply at a Disability Service Centre in your province or in Bangkok with your disability ID card or certificate, a bank book and a copy of the applicant’s ID. There is a home visit, then a committee decides. Disabled persons hotline: 1479; social assistance hotline: 1300.

emergency.label: Police and emergency line. Calls to 113 asking for medical help are passed to health staff on duty, who can send an emergency medical team

resources.name: Ngày Mai hotline
resources.what: Free psychological first aid and emotional support by phone from volunteers. It is not open around the clock; in an emergency, call 113.
resources.how: Call 096 306 1414, Wednesday to Sunday, 13:00 to 20:30. In Vietnamese; English is also listed.

resources.name: Monthly social allowance for people with disabilities (trợ cấp xã hội hàng tháng)
resources.org: People’s Committee of your commune or ward
resources.what: A monthly payment for people with disabilities who qualify, worked out from the national social assistance base rate of 500,000 dong a month (since 1 July 2024). Provinces can set a higher rate.
resources.how: Apply at the one-stop desk (bộ phận một cửa) of the People’s Committee where you live, in person, by post or online where offered, with the application form, your ID card and your disability certificate (giấy xác nhận khuyết tật). There is no fee. In Vietnamese.

emergency.label: Police, fire and medical emergencies (SAME 105) anywhere in the country, through one command centre. There is also a 9-1-1 app

resources.name: Suicide prevention line (Línea de prevención del suicidio)
resources.org: Government of Uruguay (Ministry of Public Health)
resources.what: A free, confidential line open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, answered by professionals such as psychologists and nurses. It offers listening, support and information, and arranges help in an emergency.
resources.how: Call 0800 0767 from any phone, or *0767 from a mobile, free, at any hour. In Spanish.
resources.phone_note: From a mobile you can also dial *0767.

resources.name: Disability pension (pensión por invalidez)
resources.what: A monthly pension for people with a total incapacity, as assessed by a BPS doctor, who have lived in Uruguay for at least 10 of the last 20 years (children are exempt from this). With a severe incapacity finding there is no means test; otherwise your own and your family’s income is checked.
resources.how: Apply at a BPS branch, weekdays 9:15 to 16:00, or ask by phone: 0800 1997 from a landline or *1997 from a mobile, weekdays 8:00 to 18:00. In Spanish.

resources.name: National Human Rights Institution and Ombudsman (INDDHH)
resources.org: Institución Nacional de Derechos Humanos y Defensoría del Pueblo
resources.what: Anyone can bring a complaint to the INDDHH, free of charge, when their rights have been violated, including through discrimination. It also runs a monitoring mechanism on disability issues.
resources.how: Call (598 2) 1948, email denuncias@inddhh.gub.uy, or visit Bv. Artigas 1532, Montevideo; complaints are taken weekdays 10:00 to 16:00. The number shown is for urgent complaints. In Spanish.

emergency.label: Cuerpo Voluntario de Bomberos (volunteer firefighters), for medical and other emergencies

resources.name: 1582 Te Escucha
resources.org: FUNDEGUA (Fundación Desarrolla Guatemala para la Educación y la Salud)
resources.what: A free crisis and suicide prevention line, open 24 hours a day since 10 October 2026, with referrals to other services.
resources.how: Call 1582, or send a WhatsApp message to 3007-1582. It is free for the caller.

resources.name: IGSS disability pension (pensión por invalidez)
resources.what: A pension for insured workers whose disability is confirmed by the IGSS. If it is caused by illness, you need 36 contributions paid in the 6 years before the disability began; if it is caused by an accident, you must have been covered when it happened and have 3 months of contributions in the 6 months before.
resources.how: Bring your DPI and the completed work history form (IVS-102) to the IGSS at 7.ª avenida 22-72, zona 1, Centro Cívico, Guatemala City; in the metropolitan area, book through CATAFI, and elsewhere go to your nearest IGSS office. Update your details, including your NIT, first. It is free and you do not need a lawyer or agent. In Spanish.

emergency.label: The free European emergency number; tell the operator exactly where you are. Deaf or hard of hearing people can send an SMS to the police on +36 20 9000 107

resources.name: Telephone emotional first aid (Lelki Elsősegély Telefonszolgálat) 116-123
resources.what: Someone to talk to when you are in crisis or need emotional support, 24 hours a day, every day.
resources.how: Call 116-123, at any hour. It is free from every network inside Hungary. In Hungarian. You can also write in English to the email address the association gives on its site; it says it replies within 72 hours.

resources.name: MEOSZ (National Federation of Associations of People with Physical Disabilities)
resources.what: A national federation that speaks up for people with mobility impairments: it puts proposals on benefits to the government and has reported to the Ombudsman on wheelchair access to trains.
resources.how: Call 06-1-388-2387 or 06-1-388-2388, email meosz@meosz.hu, or write to 1032 Budapest, San Marco u. 76. The site does not list opening hours. In Hungarian.

emergency.label: The single emergency number for police, ambulance, fire, mountain rescue and sea rescue, free and open 24 hours a day by phone or text message. You can report an emergency in Croatian, English, German, Italian, Hungarian or Slovak

resources.name: Plavi telefon helpline (Linija pomoći Plavi telefon)
resources.what: A free helpline for children, young people and adults anywhere in Croatia. It is not open around the clock.
resources.how: Call 01 4833 888, Monday to Friday 09:00 to 20:00. In a crisis outside those hours, call 112. The website is in Croatian.

resources.name: Inclusive allowance (inkluzivni dodatak)
resources.org: Croatian Institute for Social Work (Hrvatski zavod za socijalni rad)
resources.what: A monthly payment that helps disabled children and adults take part in society on an equal basis. It is paid at five levels of support: €720, €480, €432, €162 or €138 a month, depending on the degree of disability. It is not paid to people living in a care home or organised housing, or to people receiving the personal disability allowance (osobna invalidnina) or certain care allowances.
resources.how: Apply to the regional office (područni ured) of the Croatian Institute for Social Work. The Institute sets your level of support after an assessment by the Institute for Medical Expertise (Zavod za vještačenje). The government page is in Croatian.

resources.name: Ombudsperson for Persons with Disabilities (Pravobranitelj za osobe s invaliditetom)
resources.what: Takes individual complaints from disabled people and people acting for them. The office reviews your case, warns anyone found violating your rights and recommends how to fix it, can ask for slow proceedings to be speeded up, and tells you which institution to turn to. In cases of discrimination, violence or abuse it reports to the state attorney.
resources.how: Call 01 6102 170 or 01 6177 901, email ured@posi.hr, or write to or visit Savska cesta 41/3, 10000 Zagreb. In Croatian.

emergency.label: The single emergency number, free of charge. Deaf people and people with speech impairments can text 112. You can also call 101 for the rescue service, 102 for the police and 103 for an ambulance

resources.name: National hotline 116 123
resources.what: A free national hotline with psychological and legal consultations, for domestic violence, human trafficking and gender discrimination. La Strada-Ukraine also runs a free psychological support line for men, 2345, from 14:00 to 06:00, and a children and youth line, 0 800 500 225 or 116 111.
resources.how: Call 0 800 500 335 from a landline or mobile, or 116 123 from a mobile. You can also write on Telegram. The organisation's page does not give the hours. In Ukrainian.

resources.name: State assistance for people disabled from childhood and children with disabilities
resources.what: A monthly payment for adults disabled since childhood, for as long as the disability lasts, and for disabled children under 18. It is set as a share of the subsistence minimum: 100% for group I, 80% for group II and 60% for group III, and 70% for a child. Refugees in Ukraine can apply too. The service is free and a decision takes 10 days.
resources.how: Apply at a Pension Fund office, by registered post, or at your local administrative services centre (TsNAP). Diia's online version of the service showed as temporarily unavailable when checked. The Pension Fund's contact centre is 0 800 503 753. In Ukrainian.

resources.name: Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights (Ombudsman)
resources.what: Takes appeals about human rights, including those of disabled people; its published cases include one where a disabled person's stopped assistance was recalculated and more than 50,000 hryvnias were paid after its check.
resources.how: Call the free hotline 1678, Monday to Thursday 9:00 to 18:00 and Friday 9:00 to 16:45 (from abroad, +380 44 299 7408), or email hotline@ombudsman.gov.ua. The office warns that power cuts can briefly interrupt the line. In Ukrainian.

emergency.label: Ambulance (Saudi Red Crescent). For the police, call 999; for civil defence, call 998

resources.name: Psychological Consultation Center call line
resources.what: Connects callers anywhere in the Kingdom with mental health professionals. It is not open around the clock.
resources.how: Call 920033360, 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. (Saturdays 1:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m.). In an emergency, call 997. The Ministry's Qareboon app offers mental health counselling by text.

resources.name: Monthly financial aid, assistive devices and daily care for persons with disabilities
resources.org: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development
resources.what: Disabled people registered with the Ministry whose disability has been assessed can apply for a monthly financial aid payment, for assistive devices, and for daily social care. You can also ask for your disability assessment to be updated, appeal if your aid is stopped, and university students with disabilities can apply for a grant.
resources.how: Apply through the Ministry's e-services (eservices.hrsd.gov.sa). The Ministry's page is in Arabic.

resources.name: Traffic facilities card and transport fare discount card
resources.org: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development
resources.what: The traffic facilities card lets a disabled person enter public facility car parks and use reserved disabled spaces across the Kingdom. The fare discount card gives Saudi disabled people and their companions 50% off government transport.
resources.how: Apply on the national portal my.gov.sa: service 12346 for the traffic facilities card and service 12345 for the fare discount card. The Ministry's page is in Arabic.

emergency.label: Emergency. For an ambulance, call 912; for traffic accidents, call 113

resources.name: Health call centre 114
resources.what: RBC's mental health service tells people to call 114, its call centre with operators trained in different health fields. It is open Monday to Saturday, not around the clock.
resources.how: Call 114, Monday to Saturday. RBC's page does not give the times. In an emergency, call 112.

resources.name: National Council of Persons with Disabilities (NCPD)
resources.org: National Council of Persons with Disabilities
resources.what: The national body for disability advocacy and for including disabled people in mainstream services. Through IremboGov it issues free recommendation letters that support disabled people in taking part in activities that benefit them.
resources.how: Email info@ncpd.gov.rw, or visit the council in Kacyiru, Kigali. To get a recommendation letter, apply on IremboGov under Governance, NCPD Services, with your NCPD disability card and a document showing the reason; it takes 2 days and no Irembo account is needed.

emergency.label: Police emergency call centre, for emergencies that need an immediate response

resources.name: National Mental Health Helpline 1926
resources.what: The national mental health helpline run from the National Institute of Mental Health.
resources.how: Call 1926. The Institute's pages do not give its hours; for other questions, call the Institute on 011 2578234.

resources.name: 1990 Suwa Seriya free ambulance
resources.what: A free 24-hour emergency ambulance service covering the whole island, run by a foundation fully owned by the Government of Sri Lanka.
resources.how: Call 1990, at any hour. It is free.

resources.name: Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka (HRCSL)
resources.org: Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka
resources.what: Takes complaints from a victim or group of victims of a violation, or threatened violation, of fundamental rights, or from someone representing them.
resources.how: Call the hotline 1996, or complain in person, by post, by email to secretary@hrcsl.lk, by fax or with the online form. Complaint forms are free from the head office (14 R. A. De Mel Mawatha, Colombo 4; 011 2505580), regional offices or the website. In Sinhala, Tamil or English.

emergency.label: Police. Tourists can call the toll-free Tourist Police hotline, 1144

resources.name: National Suicide Prevention Helpline 1166
resources.org: Ministry of Health and Population, at the Mental Hospital, Lagankhel (operated by TPO Nepal with WHO support)
resources.what: Counsellors answer round the clock. Calls through the national telecom operator are free; callers on private operators pay standard rates.
resources.how: Call 1166, at any hour.

resources.name: National Federation of the Disabled Nepal (NFDN)
resources.org: National Federation of the Disabled Nepal
resources.what: The national umbrella body of organisations of persons with disabilities, with more than 350 member organisations, working to promote and protect disabled people's rights. Its site has a grievance and feedback channel.
resources.how: Call +977 1 5331159 or visit Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

emergency.label: Fire, disaster relief and ambulance, 24 hours a day

resources.name: 1925 Anxin (peace of mind) line (安心專線)
resources.what: Free psychological counselling by phone, 24 hours a day, every day of the year.
resources.how: Call 1925 from a landline or mobile, at any hour. It is free. The Ministry's page is in Chinese.

resources.name: 1957 welfare consultation line (1957福利諮詢專線)
resources.what: A free line for questions about disability welfare and other social welfare, including social assistance, emergency aid and National Pension insurance. Staff give advice and refer you on.
resources.how: Call 1957, every day 8:00 to 22:00, Lunar New Year included. Social workers speak Mandarin, Taiwanese, Hakka and English. Deaf, hard of hearing and speech-impaired people can use the LINE text service or online consultation.

emergency.label: The European emergency number. Users with disabilities can also reach emergency services by SMS to 112. Fire and rescue: 150; ambulance: 155; police: 158

resources.name: Nezábudka mental health line (Linka dôvery Nezábudka)
resources.what: Slovakia's Ministry of Justice lists Nezábudka as a mental health hotline in its important contacts for victims, and the government's child-protection centre lists it among its help lines.
resources.how: Call 0800 800 566. The official lists do not give its hours. In an emergency, call 112.

resources.name: Cash allowances to compensate for a severe disability (peňažné príspevky na kompenzáciu ŤZP)
resources.org: Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Family
resources.what: Help for people with a severe disability (ťažké zdravotné postihnutie). One-time allowances cover buying, adjusting or repairing an aid, a lifting device, buying or adapting a car, and adapting a flat, house or garage. Recurring allowances cover personal assistance, transport, increased expenses and caregiving. The severe-disability card and the parking permit are part of the same system.
resources.how: Apply at your local Office of Labour, Social Affairs and Family (Úrad práce, sociálnych vecí a rodiny); its medical assessor and a social worker assess you. Income can reduce the allowances, and none is paid if your property is worth more than 50,000 euros. In Slovak.

resources.name: Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (Komisár pre osoby so zdravotným postihnutím)
resources.org: Úrad komisára pre osoby so zdravotným postihnutím
resources.what: An independent office that examines complaints from people with disabilities who believe a Slovak authority or institution has harmed their rights.
resources.how: Submit a complaint (podnet) through the office website, call 02 2042 0309, email sekretariat@komisar.sk, or write to Račianska 153, 831 54 Bratislava. The site does not list opening hours. In Slovak.

emergency.label: The single European emergency number, for urgent help when life, health, safety or property is at risk

resources.name: National Telephone Line for Children 116 111
resources.org: Ministry of Labour and Social Policy
resources.what: A free line that works around the clock, every day. Anyone can report a child at risk, and callers can also get consultation and psychological support. It is a line about children; Bulgaria has no general adult crisis line that could be confirmed on an official page.
resources.how: Call 116 111, at any hour. It is free. Operators alert the child-protection authorities straight away when a child is at risk. In Bulgarian. For any emergency, call 112.

resources.name: Agency for People with Disabilities
resources.org: Agency for People with Disabilities (Ministry of Labour and Social Policy)
resources.what: The national agency that funds projects for rehabilitation, integration and an accessible environment, supports economic initiative by people with disabilities, and registers and oversees providers of assistive and medical devices.
resources.how: See the agency's site for its programmes and registers. The page does not give contact details.

resources.name: Ombudsman of the Republic of Bulgaria
resources.org: Ombudsman of the Republic of Bulgaria
resources.what: Takes complaints from people with disabilities about benefits and disability pensions, social services, accessible buildings, transport and public services, medical assessment of disability, municipal housing and parking, work and education.
resources.how: File a complaint with the online form, call the reception room on 02 810 6955, email priemna@ombudsman.bg, or write to 22 George Washington Str., 1202 Sofia. The page does not list reception hours.

emergency.label: Emergency, when there is an actual threat to life, health, safety, the environment or property. It works without a SIM card and with an empty account

resources.name: Vilties linija (Hope line) 116 123
resources.what: Emotional support if you are feeling mentally unwell, by phone 24 hours a day, every day. UNHCR's Lithuania help page also lists Jaunimo linija for young people (+370 800 28888, 24 hours).
resources.how: Call 116 123, at any hour. There is also an online chat in Lithuanian. If you or someone else has acute thoughts of suicide, call 112.

resources.name: Agency for the Protection of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
resources.org: Ministry of Social Security and Labour
resources.what: The state agency for the rights of persons with disabilities, under the Ministry of Social Security and Labour.
resources.how: Call +370 5 233 3320 or write to Švitrigailos St. 11E, LT-03228 Vilnius. The ministry page does not give opening hours.

resources.name: Equal Opportunities Ombudsperson
resources.org: Office of the Equal Opportunities Ombudsperson
resources.what: Investigates discrimination complaints, including discrimination because of disability, and must answer within three months.
resources.how: Send a written complaint within three months of what happened: by the electronic form, email lygybe@lygybe.lt, post, or in person at S. Konarskis st. 35, Vilnius. Phone +370 5 205 0640, Monday to Thursday 8:00 to 17:00 and Friday 8:00 to 15:45, break 12:00 to 12:45.

emergency.label: Ambulance. Police: 192; fire: 193

resources.name: National Suicide Prevention SOS Line
resources.what: A free line for people thinking about suicide or in crisis, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
resources.how: Call 0800 309 309, at any hour. It is free. UNDP also lists Centre SRCE on 0800 300 303, every day 14:00 to 23:00. In an emergency, call 194 for an ambulance or 192 for the police.

resources.name: Commissioner for Protection of Equality
resources.what: An independent body that examines discrimination complaints, including discrimination because of disability or health condition. It can propose mediation, issue recommendations and warnings, and go to court with your consent. The procedure is free.
resources.how: Send a written, signed complaint saying who was discriminated against, how, by whom, and what evidence there is, by email to poverenik@ravnopravnost.gov.rs. Anonymous complaints are not accepted. A human rights organisation can file for you with your consent.

emergency.label: Police, fire and medical emergencies, 24 hours, with translators in several languages. Deaf people can use 992 by SMS, video call or email to 992@moi.gov.qa

resources.name: National Mental Health Helpline 16000
resources.what: The main entry point for mental health support in Qatar, open to anyone regardless of age, background or nationality. Calls are answered by mental health nurses, psychologists and psychiatrists and are fully confidential. It is not open around the clock.
resources.how: Call 16000 and choose option 4 for mental health, Saturday to Thursday 8:00 to 18:00. Outside those hours, or in an emergency, call 999.

resources.name: Law No. 22 of 2025 on Persons with Disabilities
resources.org: Ministry of Social Development and Family (MSDF)
resources.what: The law bans discrimination because of disability and requires reasonable accommodation. It covers accessible buildings and transport, education, health care and rehabilitation, digital access, and job quotas in government and private work, and it provides a disability ID card for the benefits the law sets. The Ministry of Social Development and Family oversees it.
resources.how: Contact the ministry on 16080 or info@msdf.gov.qa. The ministry also offers an online "To Whom It May Concern" certificate for people with disabilities.

emergency.label: Emergency. People with a speech or hearing impairment who have registered can send an SMS to 992; registration is free, online or at a police station

resources.name: 18111 Mental Health Support Hotline
resources.what: A government-funded hotline answered 24 hours a day, all year, giving immediate support and counselling and referring callers to the most suitable service. Since November 2025 it also offers WhatsApp messaging and scheduled call-backs.
resources.how: Call 18111, at any hour. Help is available in Cantonese, Mandarin and English, plus Hindi, Nepali, Urdu, Punjabi, Bahasa Indonesia, Tagalog, Vietnamese, Bengali and Thai.

resources.name: Social Welfare Department hotline
resources.what: The 24-hour hotline of the department that runs rehabilitation services. It gives recorded welfare information, connects you to SWD offices and social security enquiries, and puts you through to a social worker for a family crisis or emotional distress.
resources.how: Call 2343 2255. Choose a language, then press 0 for a social worker (Monday to Friday 9:00 to 17:00, Saturday 9:00 to 12:00; at other times the call goes to an outreach team run by Tung Wah Group of Hospitals). For day training or residential rehabilitation services, a school, medical or family social worker applies for you through the Central Referral System.

emergency.label: Ambulance. Police: 117; fire: 118

resources.name: Child Helpline Cambodia 1280
resources.what: UNICEF Cambodia lists this helpline among the non-governmental organisations that offer mental health support. It is a line for children; no general adult crisis line could be confirmed on an official page.
resources.how: Call 1280. UNICEF's page does not give its hours or cost. In an emergency, call 119 for an ambulance or 117 for the police.

resources.name: Disability Identification Card
resources.org: Ministry of Social Affairs, Veterans and Youth Rehabilitation (MoSVY)
resources.what: The ministry's Disability Identification Programme registers people with disabilities in a national database and gives them a card that opens access to health care, assistive devices and Family Package cash benefits. More than 360,000 people had been identified by January 2026.
resources.how: MoSVY officials carry out disability screening and registration, often together with IDPoor checks; applications are checked and approved before a card is issued.

emergency.label: Police emergency

resources.name: LifeLine/ChildLine toll-free line
resources.what: The Namibian Police list LifeLine/ChildLine's toll-free numbers among their emergency contacts, which they describe as available 24/7, confidential and with support in several languages.
resources.how: Call 116 or 106, free. The police page also lists the gender-based violence toll-free line, 061 209 5226. In an emergency, call 10111.

resources.name: Disability Grant
resources.org: Ministry of Gender Equality, Poverty Eradication and Social Welfare
resources.what: A monthly cash grant of N$1,600 for Namibian citizens or permanent residents aged 16 to 59 whom a state doctor has diagnosed as temporarily or permanently disabled. Children with disabilities can get a separate Special Maintenance Grant.
resources.how: Apply in person at any district or constituency office of the ministry, weekdays 8:00 to 17:00. Bring certified copies of your birth certificate and ID (and marriage or citizenship certificate if they apply) and the medical report from a state doctor. An official fills in the form and gives you an acknowledgement of receipt.

emergency.label: Emergency Medical Services (ambulance), 24 hours a day, every day

resources.name: Childline Botswana 116
resources.what: A toll-free helpline for children, reported by the government's Daily News in May 2025. It is not yet open around the clock, and it can also be reached on Facebook and WhatsApp. No general adult crisis line could be confirmed on an official page.
resources.how: Call 116, free, until 23:00. In a medical emergency, call 997.

resources.name: Disability cash transfer
resources.org: Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development
resources.what: A monthly cash transfer and food basket for Botswana citizens with a severe and profound disability who depend on others for care, support or getting around and whose income is below the set threshold. It began in 2015; amounts may have changed since.
resources.how: A medical assessment must confirm how severe the disability is. The government report does not say where to apply.

emergency.label: Emergency system of the National Police (Policía Nacional); use it only for real emergencies

resources.name: Línea 155 Salud Mental
resources.org: Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social
resources.what: Free, confidential, nationwide crisis line for people in psychological distress, at risk of suicide or needing urgent support, 24 hours a day all year. A team trained in crisis care, including psychologists and psychiatrists, gives emotional support and crisis intervention and refers people to specialised services.
resources.how: Call 155, at any hour. It is free. In Spanish.

resources.name: Disability certificate (Certificado de Discapacidad)
resources.org: SENADIS (Secretaría Nacional por los Derechos Humanos de las Personas con Discapacidad)
resources.what: The certificate SENADIS issues after a multidisciplinary evaluation of a sensory, physical, intellectual or speech disability. The same Portal Paraguay services include registration in the national disability register and free-travel cards for land transport.
resources.how: Register as a SENADIS user (bring a copy of your cédula to the Admissions Department; up to 20 numbers are given each day from 07:00), then ask the Disability Assessment Directorate to start the certificate. SENADIS is at Jacaranda y Yeruti, Fernando de la Mora, Monday to Friday 07:00 to 13:00. It takes 15 to 20 days after the evaluations. It can also be requested on Portal Paraguay with an electronic identity.

emergency.label: Emergency system of the National Civil Police (Policía Nacional Civil), free from any phone. Medical emergencies: 132

resources.name: Telecentro MINSAL 131 (mental health option)
resources.what: The Ministry of Health's phone line. Its mental health campaign asks anyone who feels emotionally overwhelmed to call 131 or visit the nearest health facility, and UNICEF lists option 4 for mental health and option 5 for adolescents and young people.
resources.how: Call 131, choose your area, then press 4 for mental health or 5 for adolescents and young people. The official pages do not give hours or cost. In Spanish.

resources.name: CONAIPD (National Council for the Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities)
resources.org: Consejo Nacional para la Inclusión de las Personas con Discapacidad
resources.what: The national disability council. Among its free services, it advises people with disabilities on getting their right to education and follows up with the Ministry of Education and other bodies.
resources.how: Email recepcion@conaipd.gob.sv to ask for an appointment, or go to Pol. Industrial Plan de La Laguna, Calle Circunvalación, Lote No. 20, Antiguo Cuscatlán, La Libertad, 7:30 to 15:30. It answers within 15 working days. Free. In Spanish.

emergency.label: Ambulance, police and rescue, always available and free of charge

resources.name: Emotional support helpline 116 123
resources.what: Free emotional support by phone, in Estonian, Russian and English. It is not open around the clock: counsellors answer every day from 10:00 to midnight. The state health portal adds that spiritual counsellors answer from 16:00 to 02:00.
resources.how: Call 116 123, every day 10:00 to 24:00. Outside those hours, call the victim support crisis line 116 006, which answers 24 hours a day. In an emergency, call 112.

resources.name: Victim support crisis helpline 116 006
resources.what: Crisis counselling 24 hours a day, every day, in Estonian, Russian and English. The state health portal also lists it for chat and email.
resources.how: Call 116 006 at any hour. In an emergency, call 112.

resources.name: Allowance for a person of working age with disabilities
resources.what: A monthly allowance of 29 to 100 euros for people aged 16 to old-age pension age whose severity of disability has been determined. The amount depends on the severity and on which function is affected (for example 42 euros for a moderate motor disability, 50 euros for severe and 100 euros for profound).
resources.how: Apply to the Social Insurance Board through its self-service portal, by digitally signed email, by post to Paldiski mnt 80, 15092 Tallinn, or at a customer service office. Information line: +372 612 1360.

resources.name: Gender Equality and Equal Treatment Commissioner
resources.org: Soolise võrdõiguslikkuse ja võrdse kohtlemise volinik
resources.what: An independent commissioner who advises and helps people who feel discriminated against. For disability, the Equal Treatment Act protects you in work, in related education and in membership of employee or employer associations.
resources.how: Call +372 626 9059, use the contact form on the commissioner's website, or write to Kiriku 4, Tallinn 15071.

emergency.label: Fire and rescue, police, emergency medical services and the gas emergency service, free of charge from anywhere in Latvia at any time

resources.name: Psycho-emotional support line 116123
resources.what: A telephone line for psycho-emotional support for adults, completely free and available 24 hours a day, in Latvian, Russian and English. Through it, any adult resident of Latvia can also get up to 10 free consultations with a certified psychologist.
resources.how: Call 116123 at any hour. Children and teenagers can call the Child and Adolescent Helpline 116111, and victims of crime the helpline 116006. In an emergency, call 112.

resources.name: State Medical Commission for the Assessment of Health Condition and Working Ability (VDEAVK)
resources.org: Veselības un darbspēju ekspertīzes ārstu valsts komisija
resources.what: The state medical commission for assessing health and working ability. Its page on support for persons with disabilities covers benefits for adults and for families of a child with a disability, the disabled person's parking card, free intercity public transport, exemption from vehicle operating tax and the invalidity pension, with a booklet that summarises them.
resources.how: Call +371 6761 4885 or +371 2963 2807, email pasts@vdeavk.gov.lv, use the question form on its website, or write to Ventspils iela 53, Rīga, LV-1002.

resources.name: Disability pension (invaliditātes pensija)
resources.what: A pension for socially insured people living in Latvia, below retirement age, whose disability has been determined in Latvia and who have at least three years of insurance. It is paid in full while you work. From 1 January 2026, Group III is 213 euros a month (255 euros for a disability since childhood); Groups I and II depend on past earnings and insurance, with minimums of 340.80 and 298.20 euros. Disability caused by a work accident or occupational disease is handled separately.
resources.how: Apply on the Latvija.gov.lv portal, at any VSAA customer service centre with your passport or ID card, or by email with a secure electronic signature. Applying is free and takes up to 22 working days. Apply from the date your disability is determined: a late application is paid back at most 6 months. VSAA: +371 6450 7020.

resources.name: Ombudsman of the Republic of Latvia (Tiesībsargs)
resources.what: Handles discrimination (unequal treatment without an objective reason) and the rights of people with long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments.
resources.how: Submit an application online, by email to tiesibsargs@tiesibsargs.lv (signed with a secure electronic signature), through the Latvija.lv e-address, by post, or in person at Baznīcas iela 25, Rīga, LV-1010, Monday to Friday 9:00 to 17:00.

emergency.label: The single European emergency number, free from any phone, for medical help and firefighters. Police: 113

resources.name: Emotional support helpline 116 123
resources.org: Association of Slovenian Helpline Advisers for Mental Distress
resources.what: Slovenia's telecoms regulator lists 116 123 as the emotional support helpline for people in mental distress. The child helpline 116 111 is listed beside it.
resources.how: Call 116 123. The regulator's list does not give its hours. In an emergency, call 112.

resources.name: Assistance and attendance allowance (dodatek za pomoč in postrežbo)
resources.org: Pension and Disability Insurance Institute of Slovenia (ZPIZ)
resources.what: A benefit for pensioners who need another person's help with basic daily needs, and for some people working in Slovenia who are blind, partially sighted or have a physical disability. Being blind or partially sighted, or having at least 70 percent reduced ability to move, can qualify.
resources.how: Your doctor, you, or your legal or authorised representative files the claim with ZPIZ, with your medical records; ZPIZ's website has an online form. In Slovenian.

resources.name: Advocate of the Principle of Equality (Zagovornik načela enakosti)
resources.what: An independent state body that gives independent help, advice and legal aid to people who have been discriminated against, in the public and private sectors. In its annual report, disability was among the grounds of discrimination it found, and most of its 127 recommendations concerned the rights of people with disabilities.
resources.how: Call 01 473 55 31 or write to Železna cesta 16, 1000 Ljubljana. In Slovenian.

emergency.label: The national emergency number, on call 24 hours all year round. You can also reach it by text message (SMS), the 112 Iceland app or web chat

resources.name: Red Cross helpline 1717 (Hjálparsíminn 1717)
resources.what: A confidential phone line and web chat for anyone who needs someone to talk to, about anything causing concern, including anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts, abuse and loneliness. Open 24 hours and free; ask to speak English if you do not speak Icelandic.
resources.how: Call 1717 at any hour, or use the web chat. In an emergency, call 112.

resources.name: Disability pension (örorkulífeyrir)
resources.what: For people aged 18 to 67 assessed, through an integrated expert assessment, as able to take part in the labour market to only 0 to 25 percent. The full pension before tax is 416,950 krónur a month, or 486,076 with the household allowance; income above 105,200 krónur a month reduces it. People already on a disability pension can ask to move to a partial disability pension.
resources.how: Your doctor sends a medical certificate to TR; the application then appears on Ísland.is for you to complete and submit, and TR's letters and decision come to My Pages. TR: 560 4400, weekdays 10:00 to 15:00, Hlíðasmári 11, 201 Kópavogur.

resources.name: Rights protection for people with disabilities (Réttindagæsla fatlaðs fólks)
resources.what: Rights advocates who protect the legal and human rights of disabled people: they look into how a case was handled, attend meetings or police questioning with you, prepare complaints and appeals, and help people who need support with legal capacity or want a personal spokesperson.
resources.how: Call 554-8100, weekdays 9:00 to 16:00 (you can leave a message outside those hours), or email rettindagaesla@mannrettindi.is.

emergency.label: Fire brigade or ambulance, free of charge, 24 hours a day, from landlines and mobiles. Police: 113

resources.name: SOS Détresse
resources.what: Psychological support by phone. Luxembourg's police list it under psychological support in their directory of help for victims.
resources.how: Call 454 545. The police list does not give its hours. In an emergency, call 112.

resources.name: Allowance for the severely disabled (RPGH)
resources.org: National Solidarity Fund (FNS) and the ADEM Medical Commission
resources.what: An income for adults living in Luxembourg whose disability is so severe that they cannot work: at least 30 percent reduced work capacity before age 65, and work either medically ruled out or impossible to adapt. Its gross amount equals the social inclusion income (REVIS); other income counts against it. Non-EU, EEA or Swiss nationals need 5 years of legal residence in the last 20.
resources.how: Get the application form from the secretariat of the Medical Commission at ADEM, then email it with a recent medical report and the other documents to commissionmedicale@adem.etat.lu. The Commission decides within 2 months, then the FNS checks age, residence and income. ADEM: 247 88 888. FNS: 49 10 81 1.

resources.name: Centre for Equal Treatment (CET)
resources.what: An independent body that promotes, analyses and monitors equal treatment without discrimination on grounds including disability, race or ethnic origin, gender, sexual orientation, religion or belief, and age.
resources.how: Email info@cet.lu, call 28 37 36 35, or write to 65, route d'Arlon, L-1140 Luxembourg. You can write in Luxembourgish, French, German or English.

emergency.label: Ambulance, fire and police

resources.name: Mental Health Helpline 1579
resources.org: Mental Health Services, Ministry for Health
resources.what: A 24-hour national helpline giving free emotional support, advice and practical guidance to anyone in need, including people in crisis and people worried about a family member or friend. It is answered by psychology professionals from Mental Health Services.
resources.how: Call 1579 at any hour. In an emergency, call 112.

resources.name: Disability Assistance and Severe Disability Assistance
resources.what: Non-contributory payments for people aged 16 to under 65 whose disability began before 60, rated by the Inter-Professional Board: 45 to 59 percent for Disability Assistance, 60 to 74 percent for Severe Disability Assistance, and 75 percent or more for Increased Severe Disability Assistance. There is no means test, so you can qualify while working. Paid every four weeks.
resources.how: Your treating specialist applies for you through the online Medical Report form; the Inter-Professional Board then assesses you.

resources.name: Report disability discrimination to the CRPD
resources.org: Commission for the Rights of Persons with Disability (CRPD)
resources.what: People with disabilities, and family members directly affected, can report discrimination on the grounds of disability. The report is vetted within 10 days and assessed within 30, with a decision within 180 days.
resources.how: Fill in the online e-form on servizz.gov.mt.

emergency.label: The single European emergency number, for police, ambulance and fire

resources.name: Cyprus Samaritans
resources.what: Emotional support for adults aged 18 and over. The Youth Board of Cyprus lists it among free helplines.
resources.how: Call 8000 7773 (free). The official list does not give its hours. Children and teenagers can call 116111. In an emergency, call 112.

resources.name: Commissioner for Administration and the Protection of Human Rights (Ombudsman)
resources.org: Office of the Commissioner for Administration and the Protection of Human Rights
resources.what: Examines complaints of discrimination, including when a public or private body violates your rights (for example to employment, education or health care) because of disability. You can complain for yourself or, with their consent, for someone else. It is free.
resources.how: Use the online form, email ombudsman@ombudsman.gov.cy, or deliver or post your complaint (2 Diagorou, Nicosia). Call 22 405500 to check whether the Office can look into your complaint.

emergency.label: Emergency

resources.name: Al Masarra Hospital psychiatric emergency
resources.what: The Ministry of Health's psychiatric hospital in Muscat, open around the clock. Its emergency department supports people in a mental health crisis or with addiction withdrawal. This is a hospital emergency line, not a counselling helpline.
resources.how: Call 2487 3268, the hospital's number for psychiatry and addiction emergencies. The hospital is in Al-Heshya, Al Amerat, Muscat Governorate. In an emergency, call 9999.

resources.name: Card for persons with disabilities
resources.what: The card is the way in to other services: with it you can request assistive devices, a disabled parking permit, vocational rehabilitation and employment opportunities. It is free and takes 14 working days.
resources.how: First get a medical examination and a medical report from a Ministry of Health centre giving the type and level of the disability and when it began. Then apply with the medical examination form, the report, the card application form and the disabled person's data form.

emergency.label: Emergency response. Fire: 101; police: 102; ambulance: 103

resources.name: 108 Child Helpline
resources.org: General Authority for Child and Family Development and Protection
resources.what: Mongolia's children's emergency line, under the Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Protection. In December 2025 the government merged child protection response services and temporary shelter into the 108 centre, which gives rapid child protection help, counselling and information. No general crisis line for adults could be confirmed on an official page.
resources.how: Call 108. The ministry's pages do not give its hours. In an emergency, call 105.

resources.name: Social welfare pension for adults with disabilities
resources.org: Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Protection
resources.what: Under the Law on Social Welfare (article 12.1.3), adults with disabilities who have lost 50 percent or more of their ability to work can get a monthly social welfare pension. The law also provides care allowances for people caring for disabled children and for citizens who need constant care.
resources.how: The law text does not say where to apply. The ministry's public relations division can be reached on +976 51 266324 or international@mlsp.gov.mn.
